findings.issue_text: [BUG] The reminder-cancellation DB writes (prisma.workflowReminder.update to set cancelled=true for EMAIL, prisma.workflowReminder.delete for SMS) now run inside fire-and-forget async calls that are never awaited, whereas the old code collected the deletes into remindersToDelete and awaited them via Promise.all(prismaPromises). In a serverless/terminating runtime the handler returns after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` while the cancellation writes are still in flight, so the cancelled=true flag (or SMS row delete) can be silently dropped — the booking is cancelled but the hourly cron never sees cancelled=true and the attendee still receives the email/SMS reminder for the cancelled booking, i.e. the exact defect this PR is meant to fix.

[BUG] Same regression as handleCancelBooking: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are invoked without await inside forEach and the previously present `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` is removed, so the cancellation DB writes are not completed before the tRPC mutation resolves. On a reschedule/cancel the cancelled flag or SMS reminder row delete can be lost when the request finishes first, leaving stale reminders that fire for a booking time that no longer exists; the old code guaranteed the writes were committed before responding.

[BUG] The per-reminder cancel loop runs inside one try/catch, so a single SendGrid failure (e.g. batch_id already expired/unknown, which SendGrid returns 404 for on /v3/user/scheduled_sends) throws, is swallowed by the console.log catch, and aborts the loop — the remaining reminders in remindersToCancel are neither cancelled via SendGrid nor deleted, and because they are never deleted the same poisoned reminder is re-selected on every cron run and blocks all subsequent ones indefinitely. One un-cancellable reminder permanently wedges the cancellation path of the hourly cron: every later cancelled booking's reminders keep firing because the loop never reaches them, and the failure is invisible except as a repeated console.log.

[BUG] The reschedule path passes immediateDelete=true, which makes deleteScheduledEmailReminder rely solely on the SendGrid cancel API call: on any error the catch in emailReminderManager swallows it and the function returns without setting cancelled=true or deleting the row, so unlike the cancel path (which flags cancelled=true for the cron as a fallback) there is no DB-level record of the cancellation intent. If the SendGrid call fails transiently during a reschedule, the reminder row stays scheduled=true/cancelled=null, the cron query (`cancelled: true`) never picks it up, and attendees receive the reminder for the old booking time even though the booking was rescheduled — a silent, unrecoverable miss.

[ADVISORY] remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => ...) keeps the async-callback-in-forEach pattern, and the new DB writes (cancelled=true flag for EMAIL, row delete for SMS inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder) are therefore not awaited by editStep before it continues and returns. The mutation response can resolve before the cancellation writes commit; the new reminders scheduled for the edited step then coexist with old reminders whose cancelled flag/delete was silently lost, so users get duplicate workflow reminders after editing a step. The next change to this code path is also riskier because completion of cancellation work is invisible at the call site.

[BUG] The deferred-cancellation design only cancels SendGrid batches at cron time for reminders with scheduledDate <= now+1h, so any booking cancelled after the last cron run before a reminder's send time still gets its reminder delivered. A booking cancelled within the final hour before a workflow reminder fires (e.g. a 1h-before-start reminder, cancellation 90 minutes before the meeting) is never picked up by the remindersToCancel query in time: the next cron run lands at or after the SendGrid send time, so attendees receive reminder emails/SMS for meetings that no longer exist. This defeats the PR's core purpose for the most common cancellation window; previously deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancelled immediately via the SendGrid API.

[BUG] The rendering gate is narrowed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, dropping the isSenderIdNeeded sibling flag with no compensating render path anywhere in this diff. A workflow step where isSenderIdNeeded is true but isPhoneNumberNeeded is false no longer renders this block, which contains the only UI for editing and verifying the step's sendTo field; users editing such steps lose the ability to change or verify the target number, and the form field silently keeps its stale value.

[BUG] The reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder fire-and-forget inside forEach and the old 'await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)' was removed, so the prisma.workflowReminder.update that sets cancelled:true is no longer awaited before the tRPC response resolves. On serverless hosts the response can resolve before the unawaited prisma writes commit, leaving reminder rows with cancelled:null; the scheduleEmailReminders cron then never selects them (it only queries cancelled:true) and attendees receive reminders for a booking that was rescheduled. Before this diff the DB deletion of those reminders was explicitly awaited.

[BUG] Same regression as bookings.tsx: handleCancelBooking now relies on unawaited async calls (the prisma cancelled:true write lives inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder) and the reminders were removed from the awaited prismaPromises array. If the function responds before the fire-and-forget prisma.workflowReminder.update commits, the cancelled flag is never persisted, the cron's cancelled:true query never matches the reminder, and attendees get reminders for a cancelled booking — the exact failure the removed awaited deleteMany path prevented.

[BUG] The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without writing any durable state (no cancelled flag, no row delete), and the outer catch swallows failures, so a failed SendGrid cancel leaves the reminder scheduled with cancelled:null and no retry mechanism covers it. During reschedule (handleNewBooking) or workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx, both passing immediateDelete=true), a transient SendGrid error is reduced to a console.log; the reminder row keeps scheduled=true/cancelled=null so the cron's cancelled:true query never picks it up, and the attendee receives a reminder for the old, superseded time slot with no self-healing path.

[ADVISORY] The try/catch spans the entire per-reminder loop, so the first failing SendGrid request aborts cancellation of every remaining reminder in that run and also skips the Promise.all of queued deletes for batches already cancelled. One bad reminder (or one SendGrid outage blip) delays cancellation of all other expiring reminders by a full cron interval, during which those reminders deliver; errors are only console.logged, so operators get no structured signal that cancellations are silently failing.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten deleteScheduledEmailReminder now has three distinct behavior branches (null-referenceId delete, immediateDelete cancel-only, deferred cancelled-flag) and none of the new branching, the new cron cancellation loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, or the reschedule-time cancellation in handleNewBooking.ts is covered by any test in this diff. A scan of the diff finds no test-shaped files (spec/**, test/**, *.test.*, *.spec.*) exercising any of this; a regression in any branch (e.g. the null-referenceId early return, or the cancelled:true flag write) would silently re-enable reminders for cancelled bookings across all lifecycle paths, which is precisely the failure class this PR exists to fix.

[ADVISORY] The immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the database with scheduled=true and cancelled=null forever, and the new cron reaper only deletes rows where cancelled:true, so immediate-path rows have no cleanup path at all. Every reschedule (handleNewBooking) accumulates dead reminder rows on the old booking that no query in this diff ever reaps; any consumer treating scheduled=true as 'this reminder will fire' (including the deferred-cancellation cron itself, which would re-cancel an already-cancelled batch if the flag were later set) operates on stale state, and row volume grows unboundedly with reschedule traffic.

[ADVISORY] The same lifecycle event (reschedule) uses two different cancellation strategies: handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true (synchronous SendGrid cancel) while this tRPC reschedule path omits the flag and defers to the cancelled-flag cron. Whether an attendee stops receiving reminders for the old slot immediately or only after the next cron pass (with the final-hour gap of the scheduleEmailReminders finding) depends on which endpoint performed the reschedule, so the two entry points behave inconsistently and the tRPC path inherits the deferred path's late-cancellation hole unnecessarily.

[ADVISORY] The try/catch around the forEach of reminder cancellations is dead code: the delete functions swallow their own errors internally and forEach returns synchronously, so the catch can never observe a rejection from this block. Future maintainers will assume failures in cancelling old reminders during reschedule are handled here (the log.error line suggests it), when in fact every failure is silently reduced to a console.log inside the managers; the misleading handler makes the next change to this block likelier to keep relying on error handling that does not exist.

[BUG] The try/catch added around reminder cancellation in the reschedule path wraps a forEach of un-awaited async calls, so it can never catch the errors it exists to catch. deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async; their rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections after the forEach returns, the log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders") line is dead code, and a failed cancellation is silently lost so the old booking's reminder still fires.

[BUG] The refactor drops the invariant that all reminder cleanup completes (and surfaces errors) before the cancel handler returns: the previous remindersToDelete array awaited via Promise.all is replaced by fire-and-forget async calls inside forEach. SMS reminder DB deletes now run unawaited in the background and any Twilio or Prisma failure is swallowed by the console.log catch instead of propagating as before; orphaned WorkflowReminder rows can outlive the cancelled booking with no error surfaced to the caller or logs above console level.

[BUG] Same dropped invariant in the trpc reschedule mutation: the `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` barrier was removed and replaced by un-awaited async forEach calls. The mutation responds before SMS reminder rows are deleted or email flags are written; failures in deleteScheduledSMSReminder/deleteScheduledEmailReminder are no longer propagated to the client as before (the old code's unhandled rejection would reject the awaited Promise.all), leaving stale rows that reference the rescheduled-from booking.

[BUG] If twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) throws, the prisma.workflowReminder.delete in the same try block never executes, so the DB row survives a failed cancellation — the old callers deleted the row independently of the provider call. A transient Twilio failure leaves the reminder row in place with the SMS not cancelled, so the SMS still fires for the cancelled/rescheduled booking and the orphaned row is never cleaned up by any code path in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Roughly 75 lines of JSX re-indentation plus a condition narrowing from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` land in this PR with no traceable connection to the stated reminder-lifecycle requirement. Reviewers of the reminder-cancellation logic must diff through an unrelated UI refactor to find it, and the silent removal of the isSenderIdNeeded branch changes which steps render the phone-verification container (previously rendered empty when only senderId was needed) without any requirement or changelog covering it; future blame on the verification UI now points at a reminder PR.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated wholesale re-indentation of the preview-booking block (code moved from nested indentation to column 0) is included in this reminder-management PR. The diff inflates with churn that no requirement accounts for, and the resulting formatting (nested if/else bodies at column 0) actively misleads readers about block structure, making the next edit to this preview code riskier.

[ADVISORY] The new three-branch cancellation behavior (null referenceId → delete, immediateDelete → SendGrid cancel, default → set cancelled=true) plus the cron-side consumer of the cancelled flag have no test anywhere in this diff. A regression in the cancelled=true write or in the scheduleEmailReminders.ts query would mean cancelled/rescheduled bookings keep receiving email reminders, and nothing in CI would fail — the entire safety net this PR introduces is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new cancellation sweep awaits SendGrid calls sequentially inside one loop guarded by a single broad catch, so the first failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in the batch, and errors are logged with console.log instead of the logger used elsewhere in the workflow code. One bad reminder (e.g. a referenceId SendGrid no longer recognizes) permanently blocks every cancelled reminder behind it in each cron run until it is somehow removed, and the failure is invisible to any log aggregation keyed on the structured logger.

[ADVISORY] The remindersToCancel query has no filter on referenceId being non-null and no bound on result size, and a reminder whose SendGrid cancel already succeeded once but whose row delete failed will be re-selected and re-cancelled on every cron run forever. A reminder row that fails to delete after a successful SendGrid cancel (or one with a stale batch_id that SendGrid rejects) re-enters the sweep every run — cancelled=true rows with past scheduledDate always match `scheduledDate lte now+1hour` — producing a permanent per-run retry against SendGrid with no cap, backoff, or dead-lettering.

[BUG] Reminder cancellation was converted from awaited Prisma deletes (collected into prismaPromises and awaited via Promise.all) to fire-and-forget async calls inside forEach, with no await anywhere for deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder. The handler resolves as soon as Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) completes; on a serverless host (Cal.com's primary deployment) the lambda can be frozen after the response before the flag-write (email) or the Twilio cancel + prisma delete (SMS) ever execute, so attendees of a cancelled booking still receive reminders and the WorkflowReminder rows are never cleaned up. The old code guaranteed completion by awaiting remindersToDelete.

[BUG] The reschedule path dropped 'await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)' entirely: the EMAIL/SMS dispatch now invokes unawaited async managers inside forEach and the collected-then-awaited Prisma deleteMany batch was removed. The tRPC mutation returns before any reminder is cancelled or any row deleted; if the process is recycled after the response (serverless/edge restarts), the old booking's SMS reminders still fire via Twilio and the email rows never get flagged cancelled, reproducing reminders for a booking that no longer exists.

[BUG] In the workflow activeOn-update path, the awaited 'await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)' was deleted and replaced by unawaited async manager calls inside forEach. Disabling event types on a workflow returns success while none of the SendGrid cancels, Twilio cancels, or DB flag-writes have been awaited; a process recycle after the response leaves every disabled reminder scheduled and delivering to bookings the user believes are unsubscribed.

[BUG] The reschedule path permanently destroys the original booking's reminders (SMS rows deleted via prisma, email batches cancelled with immediateDelete=true) before eventManager.reschedule runs, with no compensation if the reschedule fails. When reschedule throws (e.g., no available slot, integration failure), the handler errors out but the original booking remains confirmed with its reminders gone: the attendee silently stops receiving the SMS reminder (rows hard-deleted) and email reminders for a booking that is still live. Old code made no reminder changes on this path until the new booking was secured.

[BUG] The cancellation loop is a single try/catch around the whole for-loop: the first failing SendGrid cancel aborts iteration, skips the Promise.all of already-queued deletes, and never deletes the failing reminder row. One poison reminder (e.g., a batch_id SendGrid already dispatched or expired because the cron was down past the 1-hour window) permanently fails cancellation, is never deleted, and is re-fetched and retried on every cron run forever — while also aborting the loop so all later cancelled reminders in that run are never processed. A single bad row degrades the entire cancellation pipeline with no dead-letter or per-item error handling.

[BUG] Email-reminder cancellation correctness is now delegated to the scheduleEmailReminders cron (flag 'cancelled' is only honored by this endpoint's new query), replacing the previous synchronous cancel-at-source design. On any deployment where this endpoint is not wired to a scheduler (self-hosted installs must configure it separately), cancelled=true rows are never cancelled with SendGrid and never deleted — attendees of cancelled bookings keep receiving email reminders, a regression from the old synchronous deleteScheduledEmailReminder that cancelled and deleted inline. Even with the cron, cancellation latency is now bounded only by cron frequency, not by the user's cancel action.

[ADVISORY] The new remindersToCancel findMany has no LIMIT/pagination and its results are processed with sequential awaited SendGrid HTTP calls inside a for-loop. A backlog of cancelled reminders (e.g., after a bulk booking cancellation or cron downtime) materializes fully in memory and issues one serial external API call per row, which can exceed the cron invocation window and starve the scheduling half of the same handler; the batch shrinks only one cron run at a time.

[ADVISORY] The new 'cancelled' column is a nullable BOOLEAN with no DEFAULT(false), making the flag tri-state (true/null/false). Every consumer must remember that null means 'not cancelled'; the first future query written as where: { cancelled: false } (the natural negation) silently excludes all pre-existing and default rows, and any NOT NULL/data-integrity tooling treats the column as optional. The migration also adds no index, so the cron query filtering on cancelled + scheduledDate does a full table scan as the table grows.

[ADVISORY] The old code scoped reminder deletion to the owner ('where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } }'); the replacement deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder delete/update by bare reminder.id with no ownership re-check. The delete path's ownership guard now rests entirely on whatever where-clause the upstream remindersToDeletePromise fetch uses; any future caller that passes reminders from a less-scoped query gets an unscoped cross-user delete/update of reminder rows (authz depth to be confirmed by the Security lens, but the scoped-delete defense was removed in this diff).

[ADVISORY] The immediateDelete=true branch cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, while the immediateDelete=false branch flags it and the referenceId=null branch deletes it — three exit paths, only two of which touch the DB. The handleNewBooking reschedule path (the only immediateDelete=true caller in this diff) leaves the old booking's reminder rows behind as scheduled=true, cancelled=null with dead referenceIds; no code in this diff removes them, so rows accumulate per reschedule until some out-of-diff cleanup runs, and any future reader of booking.workflowReminders sees stale 'scheduled' reminders for a cancelled batch.

[ADVISORY] The same EMAIL/SMS dispatch block (method check + manager call) is now hand-copied at seven call sites across four files, and the copies already disagree on the immediateDelete argument (true for workflow-delete and step-edit, false/omitted for booking cancel, reschedule, and disable). The next workflow-reminder change (e.g., adding a third method or fixing the await semantics) must be replicated in seven places, and the divergent immediateDelete values show the copies are already drifting; a single cancelWorkflowReminders(reminders, opts) helper would collapse all of them and make the await/flag semantics impossible to get wrong per-site.

[BUG] Reminder cancellation calls in handleCancelBooking are fired without await and were removed from the awaited prismaPromises array, so the handler responds before cancellation work completes. The old code collected reminder deletions into prismaPromises and awaited them via Promise.all; the new code calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach with no await and no promise collection. On a serverless host the process can freeze right after the response, so the 'cancelled=true' flag write (email) or the Twilio cancel + row delete (SMS) never lands — the cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts only cancels rows flagged cancelled=true, so attendees of a cancelled booking still receive reminders that the PR's stated intent says must be cancelled.

[BUG] The reschedule path fires reminder-cancellation promises without awaiting them after removing the old 'await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)'. Old code awaited all reminder deletions before proceeding; the new forEach invokes the async delete helpers with no await and no collection. The tRPC mutation can complete (and in serverless the isolate can suspend) before the cancelled flag is persisted or the SMS row/Twilio cancellation happens, so reminders for the superseded booking slot can still be delivered even though the DB mutation reported success.

[BUG] The new cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch, so the first failing SendGrid call aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders and skips awaiting every collected prisma delete. One client.request failure (e.g. one stale/invalid batch_id returning 4xx) throws, jumps to the catch that only console.logs, and the for-loop stops: every subsequent reminder with cancelled=true and scheduledDate within the next hour is neither cancelled at SendGrid nor deleted, and the already-collected workflowRemindersToDelete promises are never awaited (leaking unhandled rejections). Attendees of many cancelled bookings silently receive reminders; the error is reduced to a console.log on the next run, where the same first-failing reminder may abort the loop again indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] The semantics of deleteScheduledEmailReminder silently changed from 'cancel at SendGrid + delete row' to three divergent behaviors selected by an immediateDelete flag, and the immediateDelete=true branch neither deletes nor flags the WorkflowReminder row. Call sites now get three different contracts under one name: no referenceId → DB delete only; immediateDelete → SendGrid cancel but the DB row survives as scheduled=true/cancelled=null forever; default → flag only, actual SendGrid cancel deferred to the cron. The orphaned rows from the immediateDelete path (handleNewBooking reschedule, workflow/step deletion survivors before cascade) are invisible to the cron (it only selects cancelled=true), accumulate unboundedly, and are re-iterated on every later lifecycle event touching that booking. Whoever changes any call site next must reverse-engineer which of the three behaviors they need — the next change gets riskier because the name no longer describes any of the branches.

[ADVISORY] The default (non-immediateDelete) path replaces the previous synchronous cancellation guarantee with eventual cancellation that depends entirely on the scheduleEmailReminders cron running at least once per hour. Old code cancelled the SendGrid batch synchronously in the cancel/reschedule API path; new code only writes cancelled=true and relies on the cron query (scheduledDate lte now+1h). A reminder scheduled shortly after the booking is cancelled or rescheduled — e.g. one firing within the gap between cancellation and the next cron tick — can still be delivered, and any deployment where the cron is down, misconfigured, or runs slower than hourly silently reverts to the exact bug this PR claims to fix ('cancel reminders for cancelled bookings'). Self-hosted operators who never wired up the scheduleEmailReminders endpoint lose the guarantee entirely, with no signal that cancellation is deferred infrastructure work rather than a completed API call.

[ADVISORY] The new try/catch with log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') in the reschedule path is dead error handling: both delete helpers swallow their own errors via console.log and the async calls are not awaited. If cancellation of the previous booking's reminders fails, the error is swallowed inside emailReminderManager/smsReminderManager with a bare console.log, the log.error line never executes, and the reschedule proceeds as if cancellation succeeded — stale reminders for the old slot can fire with no application-level log or metric to notice. The catch block cannot catch anything from these fire-and-forget async calls, so it gives reviewers a false impression that failures here are handled and surfaced.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated UI behavior change — dropping isSenderIdNeeded from the phone-number block's render condition — is bundled without stated intent into a PR about reminder lifecycle management. For a workflow step where a sender ID is needed but no custom phone number is, the gray container that previously rendered (an empty box under the old outer condition) no longer renders at all; this visual change for sender-ID-only configurations ships inside a backend-reminders PR where it will not be looked for, and if it is actually a fix it is undocumented and unreviewable against the PR's stated objective.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds non-trivial new behavior-bearing logic — the deferred-cancel query, the per-reminder SendGrid cancel loop, and the three-branch deleteScheduledEmailReminder state machine — with no test anywhere in the diff. The core correctness property of this PR (a cancelled/rescheduled booking's reminders stop firing) now depends on an untested query (cancelled=true + scheduledDate window) and an untested three-way branch; a regression in any branch — e.g. the immediateDelete flag flipped, or the scheduledDate window widened — would silently resend reminders to attendees of cancelled bookings and nothing in CI would catch it.

[BUG] The edit handler's reminder teardown lost its ownership scope: the deleted code deleted reminders with `deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } } })`, but the replacement calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`, which issue `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminder.id } })` (emailReminderManager.ts / smsReminderManager.ts) with no user or booking filter. Any reminder row that reaches this loop through a fetch path without its own user scope is now hard-deleted and its SendGrid batch cancelled regardless of which user's booking it belongs to — the previous per-delete tenant scoping that guaranteed cross-tenant deletion could not happen is gone, so correctness of authorization now depends entirely on fetch queries not visible in this diff.

[ADVISORY] A new globally-scoped, destructive bulk operation (unbounded `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, ... } })` followed by SendGrid cancel calls and unconditional `workflowReminder.delete` by bare id) was added to the scheduleEmailReminders cron API endpoint, and the diff shows no authentication or secret check gating the new code path. If the endpoint is reachable without the cron secret (its only protection would be pre-existing code outside this diff), any unauthenticated caller drives third-party SendGrid API calls and hard DB deletes for every cancelled reminder due within the hour, at attacker-controlled volume — an amplified cost/rate-limit and data-deletion surface on an endpoint whose blast radius was previously limited to scheduling.

[BUG] The previous code awaited reminder deletion via Promise.all(remindersToDelete), but the refactored code invokes deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside a forEach without awaiting them, so all SendGrid/Twilio API calls and the prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete writes are fire-and-forget. The handler responds after Promise.all([attendeeDeletes, bookingReferenceDeletes].concat(apiDeletes)) completes, but the reminder cancellations (which now contain the only DB write — the cancelled:true flag or the row delete) run unawaited; on serverless/lambda runtimes the process can be frozen after the response before those promises resolve, so reminders for cancelled bookings are never marked cancelled in the DB and the cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts never sees them, meaning cancelled bookings still receive workflow reminder emails/SMSs. Internal try/catch in the managers also swallows any failure with only a console.log, so nothing surfaces the loss.

[BUG] The rescheduleMutation removed the `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` that previously guaranteed reminder cancellation completed, and the replacement forEach calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The tRPC mutation resolves (and the response is sent) before the Twilio cancelSMS calls and prisma.workflowReminder.delete writes execute; if the serverless invocation is frozen after the response, the old booking's SMS reminders are never cancelled at Twilio nor deleted from the DB, so attendees receive reminders for a booking slot they already rescheduled. The old code guaranteed these DB deletions finished before returning; the new code guarantees nothing.

[ADVISORY] A single try/catch wraps the entire per-reminder cancellation loop, so the first client.request failure (e.g., one SendGrid 4xx) aborts the loop and skips the SendGrid cancel plus the prisma delete for every remaining reminder in remindersToCancel. One failing reminder leaves all subsequent cancelled:true reminders unprocessed — they are never cancelled at SendGrid and never deleted, so emails for already-cancelled bookings still go out on that cron run, and rows cancelled before the failure accumulate in the DB forever because the Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete) is also skipped. Per-reminder error handling (continue-on-error) is needed for a batch cron; the current structure makes one bad row poison the whole hourly batch.

[BUG] Reminder cancellation was converted from awaited Prisma deletes into unawaited async calls (deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder return promises that nothing awaits), so the handler can return before any cancel or DB write completes. On a serverless/short-lived runtime the process is frozen after the response, so SendGrid/Twilio cancels never fire and email reminders are never marked cancelled=true (the new cron's cleanup key) — cancelled bookings still receive reminder emails and the reminder rows linger forever; the old code guaranteed the DB deletes via `await Promise.all(prismaPromises...)`.

[BUG] The reschedule path fires reminder cancellation inside a plain forEach with no await, and the previously-awaited `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed, so no reminder cleanup is awaited before the mutation resolves. The tRPC mutation can complete (and the request lifecycle end) before the Twilio/SendGrid cancels or the DB row deletions run, leaving scheduled reminders for the old booking live and their rows un-deleted; rejections from the cancel calls also become unhandled promise rejections instead of surfaced errors, as the old awaited deletes guaranteed.

[BUG] In the activeOn-update path the reminder cancel calls are fired in a forEach with no await, and the awaited `Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)` block was deleted, so the old reminders' DB rows are neither deleted nor marked cancelled before the mutation returns. When a user disables event types on a workflow, the old scheduled reminders survive the request (rows stay scheduled=true, cancelled=null), the new cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts never picks them up (it only processes cancelled=true), so reminders fire for event types the user turned off.

[BUG] In the step-edit path `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => ...)` launches async cancel/delete promises that nothing awaits, replacing the previously-awaited `deleteMany`, so step-edit cancellation is fire-and-forget. Editing a workflow step can return before the old reminders are cancelled or marked cancelled=true; the unawaited cancels may never execute, leaving stale reminders that fire with the old template/time, and any rejection surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of being handled.

[BUG] The new try/catch around `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)... })` cannot catch anything because the async functions' rejections are not awaited inside the synchronous forEach callback, making the `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders", error)` handler dead code. Failures cancelling the previous booking's reminders never reach the intended log/handling path — they escape as unhandled promise rejections — and cancellation is unawaited, so the old reminders can survive into the rescheduled booking and fire redundantly.

[BUG] The `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch but performs no database write (no delete and no `cancelled: true` update), so callers that pass `true` — e.g. handleNewBooking.ts's reschedule path — leave the previous booking's WorkflowReminder rows in place with scheduled=true and cancelled=null. Every reschedule orphans the prior booking's reminder rows permanently: the new cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts only deletes rows with cancelled=true, and the reschedule flow never revisits old bookings' rows, so WorkflowReminder grows without bound and stale rows are repeatedly re-fetched (e.g. via remindersFromStep on later step edits) as if they were live.

[BUG] The Prisma delete is now gated behind a successful `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` inside the same try block, so if the Twilio call throws, the row is never deleted and the error is swallowed — unlike the old flow, which deleted the reminder row regardless of the Twilio outcome. A transient Twilio failure leaves the WorkflowReminder row in place with no retry path (the new cron only cleans up cancelled email rows, and SMS rows are never soft-cancelled), so orphaned SMS reminder rows accumulate; the SMS itself may also still fire since the cancel failed and nothing retries it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch but never updates or deletes the WorkflowReminder row, unlike the SMS path (deletes the row) and the soft path (sets cancelled), leaving rows with scheduled=true and cancelled=null forever. Orphaned rows accumulate on every reschedule/step-delete; when such a booking is later cancelled, the stale row re-enters the soft-cancel pipeline and the cron re-issues a SendGrid cancel for an already-cancelled batch — duplicate remote calls that feed directly into the poison-pill abort behavior in scheduleEmailReminders.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` has an `immediateDelete` branch that POSTs a SendGrid cancel and then `return`s without any Prisma update/delete of the `WorkflowReminder` row (diff: `if (immediateDelete) { await client.request(...cancel...); return; }`). By contrast, the non-immediate path sets `cancelled: true`, and the SMS path deletes the row. The new cron-like logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only cleans up rows where `cancelled: true`, cancelling remotely and then deleting the row. Therefore, reminders cancelled via `immediateDelete` are left in the DB and will not be deleted by the new cleanup path, causing orphaned rows and enabling later duplicate cancellation attempts when other code paths call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., immediateDelete=false)` (which will mark `cancelled: true` and trigger the cron cancel+delete). This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness/data-consistency defect.
